游戏的底子非常不错，各个元素相互配合能达成的上限非常高，但是！也深刻说明了——游戏制作人一定要玩甚至会玩自己的游戏！可惜很显然小丑牌的作者是个管生不管养的“父母”，有没有看看自己设计的难度等级？减弃牌数、增加经济压力、易腐永恒破坏build，甚至还有该死的租用词条，自己有没有玩过金注呢？本来商店贩卖的槽位就少的可怜，出一个核心小丑看一眼易腐、租用就能直接气笑。而且这byd牌局只有一条命没有容错，发育机会少得可怜只能战战战，一个商店烂了直接似了，金注难度下一些过渡小丑不抓就死，万一上面还带永恒就是纯纯的赤使享受。真的烂完了，最后被迫所有套路转高牌、对子，瞬间变成平平无奇的烂游、路边一条。有这么多可以优化的地方让这个本有无穷潜力的游戏焕发耀人的光彩，怎么就摊上了这样不优化也不更新的作者？真是让人意难平。

[b]My Playtime:[/b] 229.5h (100% achievement, finished the game for too many times to count) [list][*][i]First run[/i]: 3.1h [*][i]All decks in the easiest difficulty and all challenges[/i]: 38.2h [*][i]Completionist++ and Completionist+ except black deck[/i]: 228.3h [*][i]Completionist+[/i]: 229.5h[/list] [b]Grindy Achievement(s):[/b] Yes (2 achievements). [b]Optional Achievement(s):[/b] Yes (27 achievements). [b]Difficult Achievement(s):[/b] No. [h1]Intro[/h1] [i]Balatro[/i] is a card game where you play [i]Poker[/i] hands. The goal is to score as high as possible to fulfill the score needed to pass each round. The game can be played almost endlessly, up to naneinf at round ~73, although the official end is at around round 24. [b]Pros:[/b] - 15 decks with different playing styles - Challenges to prolong your playtime [b]Cons:[/b] - Can get boring if played continuously - Takes time to learn (and get addicted to) [b]Specs[/b] AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, 16GB RAM, AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT [h1]Should you buy this game?[/h1] [i]If you enjoy playing card games and doing maths, this game is for you, although the game can be quite expensive if you are not aiming for 100% or intending to play it for a long time.[/i] [hr][/hr] [h1]In-Depth Review[/h1] [h3]The Game[/h3] [b]Gameplay[/b] Assume that you are playing a single-player poker. Your goal is to play poker hands to get enough scores to finish a round. That is [i]Balatro[/i]. [i]Balatro[/i] provides 15 decks, each with different effects. Red deck allows you to discard more times, blue deck allows you to play more poker hands, and many more. Some decks make the game easier, others make it harder. At the beginning, you can only play with the red deck, and more will unlock as you finish the game with more decks or do it at a higher difficulty. Scoring is done by poker hands. Each hand gives different chips and multiplier amounts, with rarer hands giving a higher payout. Increasing these chips and mults is the main meat of the game, and can be done through many ways. Planet cards can increase your poker hand level, which will increase both chips and mults by a small amount. Some joker cards can also increase them, with or without a special condition. Some tarot cards can upgrade your cards to give some chips or mults. Despite the various ways to increase it, using all of them is vital if you want to survive, especially in the higher difficulties. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3563958615 There are 150 Joker cards in the game, each having different effects. Some can give you more money, which you can spend in the shop to buy upgrades, some can increase your chips and/or mults, and others can give other effects. Jokers are divided into several rarities, with higher rarities usually having better effects. Most decks have 5 joker slots, which are upgradeable if you buy a certain item. Finding the right synergies between the jokers is the key to winning the game. Your build depends on RNG. Your fate will also depend on it if you are not skilled enough. After finishing each round, you'll be directed to the shops where you can spend your money—which you earn based on your performance in the last round—to buy upgrades. What's in the shop is random. There are two cards and two packs, which can contain either joker, planet, or tarot cards, and one voucher that will give additional perks to your gameplay. You can reroll them, provided that you have enough money, but what shows up will always be random. [b]Strategy[/b] [i]Balatro[/i] is all about synergies. With how randomized the shop is, you need to find a way to make one in each play. Luckily, the game has so many joker combinations that you can use, and both planet and tarot cards make it possible to win the game even without any jokers. Not using either Joker, planet, or tarot cards will cripple your run greatly, though, especially if you are playing in higher difficulties. That being said, sometimes, the synergies are not enough. The main key in every run is to have enough chips, mults, and xmults that will multiply your existing mults. However, finding one of them might be hard in some seeds, forcing you to be creative. This often turns the game into RNG, where you need to find a seed that gives you these jokers before you can win, especially if you are not skilled enough. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3454861797 Other ways, like pivoting into another build mid-run, can sometimes save your run, although this might be hard to do if you are not skilled enough. I myself usually just stick with one build and find out whether I'm making it or breaking it later. This tends to be the deciding factor of what makes the game frustrating or addictive, giving me a love-hate relationship with this game. [b]Length and Difficulty[/b] Technically, you can finish each run in 1-2h, but I nailed my first win after playing for 3.1h. I spent the rest of my playtime to 100% the game. The game seems to find ways to prolong its playtime. It has 15 decks to play with, and although each deck has a different effect, most played similarly after the first few rounds. However, you need to finish the game with a particular deck to unlock a higher difficulty level of that deck. Note that there are 8 difficulties in the game, so you can imagine the number of wins that you need to do just to unlock everything. The game also offers challenges where you have some limitations in a seeded run. It helps to learn more about the game, finding new synergies from jokers that you would never try otherwise. However, they can be boring since, again, all decks are played similarly. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3482189022 For achievement hunters, the game is painful to 100%. You need to win the game with all decks at the highest difficulty, and then win the game with all joker cards at the highest difficulty. The latter one can easily take 200h since there are 150 joker cards that appear randomly. Moreover, since the game can be very repetitive, it won't be good to attempt this in one sitting. [h1]Conclusion[/h1] [i]Balatro[/i] can be a hit or miss for some people. Those who like cards and maths will like it, while those who hate repetitiveness will hate it. You can finish all that the game has to offer in ~3h, although it demands you to play for longer. The game's nature forces you to play the game over and over, trying different synergies and cards until you find no more, or get bored and try playing it with a mod to experience everything all over again. That being said, the game is not for everyone. Achievement hunters will definitely suffer to 100% it, while players who just want to play the game a few hours a day will find it to be worthwhile. That being said, the game can be quite expensive if you only aim for the first win, so it's better to be played by those who plan to spend a longer time with this game, trying to squeeze out everything that the game has to offer.

I'm rather sad that it's not as good as I've expected. Does the game *look* great? Yes. The UI is nice. The sound is too. But the gameplay itself is meh. It's just yet another HEAVILY RNG based roguelike. I like roguelikes, probably my 3rd favorite genre, but I despise them if they're absolutely unforgiving. The only time I could forgive something like that is not even the same genre and it's Fear & Hunger where that goes well with the theme of the game. To compare with other examples, The Binding of Isaac or Cult of The Lamb - most of the time you finish with a victory and the game just waits for you to do it once again whenever you please. And they give meaningful rewards - new characters or resources needed for survival. Your skill also matters there. Even if you have awful luck, if you're cracked at the game you can still pull it through. Balatro on the other hand - There is no final victory ever. There aren't even any opponents to defeat. You're just praying to god to get good items in shop and nice card drops and then you count them. Eventually you just don't get the needed items or cards. And then that's it, you lose and there goes your progress. Back to the menu where you can start counting cards again. ????? Like, at best I assume that you just get more various cards unlocked with different effects. Awesome, next time if I'm insanely lucky I may get to use my full exodia of sparkling diarrhea which has 10x smell multiplier. (I'm sorry for this one) It shouldn't be like this, but base poker feels way more balanced and fun than this. You have more moves and control there than here. Just with a good bluff, or in another way, when you spot a bluff, you can win. Here your only counters are cards. Which, are again, RNG based. Inscryption too genuinely has it better where your strategy, skill and your opponent matters. Not just luck, and where you don't just count the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cards. I'm actually happy for the dev and stuff, but how did this end up being a contender for GOTY back in the day, exactly?

The king of deck building roguelikes. At first glance, Balatro feels almost entirely RNG. Starting off as any poker game, that’s by design. After a handful of runs, you’ll understand that this game is rooted in rewarding purposeful decision-making. It's here the game begins to open up. In this game, you build an engine centered around discovering joker combinations and manipulating your deck. Your long term goal is to optimize your hand scoring by improving your deck, jokers, and economy. Each run is unique and the decisions you make in each run feel meaningful. You’ll decide things like if spending money one round is worth losing interest next round on potentially better options in the shop. Or which planet cards to prioritize, down to crafting your deck. Balatro has varying levels of difficulty in the form of stakes and types of decks, each with different rules and conditions that make the game challenging even after hundreds of hours. Another great benefit as a deckbuilder - it's incredibly easy to put this game down at any given moment. Being able to step away to change a diaper or be Dad was a huge plus for me. 10/10 - Looking forward to what LocalThunk has cooking in the next update. Earning C++ was a blast! Pros Endless possible runs Decision-making at every turn Rewarding progression Cons No more Gold Sticker Jokers left to earn

[h1]Game for achivements hunters![/h1] Balatro is a great game until you win for the first time. It has amazing visuals, animations, and sound design. However, after my first win (which came on my second run after about two hours of playtime), I found there was no real motivation to start another run besides collecting all the achievements and unlocking every card. I really tried to find a way to enjoy the game more, but there's simply nothing beyond replaying the same gameplay loop with slightly different passive abilities or increasing the difficulty. I was genuinely hyped to play this game because of all the positive reviews and praise, but I ended up feeling very disappointed. If you enjoy collecting every achievement, then this game will most likely be for you. Personally, I don't find playing the same game over and over again just to have pointless badge(achivements) on my steam profile fun or exciting.

This was my introduction to the roguelike deckbuilder genre, drawn in by the interesting theme. It's poker, but also not at all. Addictive, technically decent game. But the gameplay is pure gambling, no skill, unless realising that squares have the biggest area of all rectangles is a skill for you. It is fun, but after playing it my mind feels numb. So I'm going to recommend against it, similar to Luck be a Landlord. It is probably more fun to watch someone else play this game. If you're looking at this game because you like poker, this has nothing to do with poker except for the starting deck (but later not even that) and being roughly inspired by poker's scoring system. It is much more luck-based than poker and completely lacks the betting element, which I believe to be the essential part of poker (but I'm not a poker player so maybe I'm wrong). Obviously this has absolutely nothing to do with roguelikes, so ignore silly Steam tags. Maybe except some minimal inventory management and some simple procedural generation but virtually every game these days have those. It's also not a deckbuilding game, because you start with a full deck and you can easily win the game without modifying the deck at all (AFAIK you have to rely on a standard deck for the first few runs because you don't even have deck manipulation unlocked at that point). If you like watching big numbers appear on your screen, I suggest a standard incremental game without gambling elements instead.
